conventions: Comments only: a typed source file gains TSDoc lines at its sites and changes nothing else. No code, type, import, blank line or existing comment changes, and no copyright year changes.
A site's rule gives the comment's text in labelled parts, in order: Summary, Remarks, @param, @returns, @throws. Type that text word for word, changing only the line breaks.

The labels Summary and Remarks are not typed. Summary text is the plain description. Remarks text goes under a @remarks tag, written as in ComponentEntityV1alpha1.ts: a ` *` line, ` * @remarks`, a ` *` line, then the text.
A ` *` line separates the description or remarks from the first @param, and @param, @returns and @throws sit on consecutive lines. `@param name - text` keeps its hyphen.

A new member or method block is multi-line, at the indentation of the line it documents: `/**`, one or more ` * text` lines, ` */`. Wrap text at 80 columns including the indentation, as Entity.ts does. Prettier does not wrap comments.
No release tag on a member or method block; it inherits from its class or interface. Only the conditions.ts blocks carry @public, on the line they already have.

TSDoc markup characters (at sign, braces, angle brackets) appear only inside backticks, as they do in the site rules. Never write a star followed by a slash inside comment text, so comment text holds no regular expression.
Wording follows docs/contribute/doc-style-guide.md: U.S. English, present tense, active voice, plain language, with code names in backticks.
The changeset follows the existing .changeset files: single-quoted package name, one plain-language paragraph for adopters, no internal symbol names.

decisions.choice: Name symbols in backticks and write no {@link} tag
decisions.reason: An unresolved link adds a warning line to the API report, which NFR-4 and AC-2 forbid, and backticks carry the same meaning.

decisions.topic: Where the type and the JSON schema differ
decisions.choice: The spec comment states what the JSON schema does and names the difference: User memberOf is required by the schema and optional in the type, and dependencyOf on Component and Resource is in the type but not in the schema
rejected: Changing the type to match the schema
decisions.reason: FR-2 requires agreement with the schema, the User tests reject a missing memberOf, and NFR-1 forbids a type change.

decisions.topic: Where the code and Kubernetes differ
decisions.choice: Validator comments state the code's rules with no comparison to Kubernetes, for example isValidObjectName accepts upper case and underscores, and isValidAnnotationValue applies no size limit
decisions.reason: FR-3 says the comment states what the code does.

decisions.choice: No unit writes a report: the orchestrator regenerates both reports after the typed files are in. FR-5 appears in the covers of U15, the last source unit, only because finalize requires every FR id to be covered
decisions.reason: Requirements FR-5 keeps the step out of the spec and a docs run holds no tooling unit. AC-1 and AC-2 are judged after that step, so they are not project checks.

decisions.choice: The project check runs `yarn lint`, without --fix
decisions.reason: A check does not write files. A pass without --fix means `yarn lint --fix` has nothing to change, which satisfies AC-7.
No .changeset markdown file names @backstage/catalog-model at the current HEAD, so nothing already covers this change.

units.behaviour: Each of the 8 isValid* static methods has TSDoc that states the rules the method applies.
rules: [PREFIX] in a site rule stands for this text: The prefix must be a DNS subdomain of 1 to 253 characters, made of dot-separated labels. Each label has 1 to 63 lowercase ASCII letters, digits and hyphens, and starts and ends with a letter or digit.
Every block ends with exactly this tag line: @param value - The value to check

sites.rule: Summary: Checks that the value is a valid entity `apiVersion`. Remarks: The value must be a string on the form `<suffix>` or `<prefix>/<suffix>`, with at most one `/`. [PREFIX] The suffix must have 1 to 63 ASCII letters or digits, in upper or lower case, and no other characters.
Summary: Checks that the value is a valid entity `kind`. Remarks: The value must be a string of 1 to 63 ASCII letters or digits, in upper or lower case, that starts with a letter.

Summary: Checks that the value is a valid object name. Remarks: The value must be a string of 1 to 63 characters. It can contain ASCII letters in upper or lower case, digits, `-`, `_` and `.`, and must start and end with a letter or digit. Separators can repeat, so `a--b` and `a..b` are valid.

Summary: Checks that the value is a valid entity namespace. Remarks: The value must be a DNS label: a string of 1 to 63 lowercase ASCII letters, digits and hyphens that starts and ends with a letter or digit. Upper case letters, `_` and `.` are not valid.

Summary: Checks that the value is a valid label key. Remarks: The value must be a string on the form `<name>` or `<prefix>/<name>`, with at most one `/`. [PREFIX] The name must satisfy `isValidObjectName`.
Summary: Checks that the value is a valid label value. Remarks: The value must be the empty string, or a string that satisfies `isValidObjectName`.

Summary: Checks that the value is a valid annotation key. Remarks: The value must be a string on the form `<name>` or `<prefix>/<name>`, with at most one `/`. [PREFIX] The name must satisfy `isValidObjectName`.
Summary: Checks that the value is a valid annotation value. Remarks: The value can be any string, including the empty string, with no limit on length or characters. Any other type is not valid.

sites.rule: Summary: Checks the format of the fields in the entity envelope, and leaves the entity unchanged. Remarks: The method checks `apiVersion`, `kind`, `metadata.name`, `metadata.namespace` if it is defined, each key and value of `metadata.labels` and `metadata.annotations`, each entry of `metadata.tags`, and the `url`, `title` and `icon` of each entry of `metadata.links`, where `title` and `icon` are optional. The validators passed to the constructor check all of these fields except those of `metadata.links`, which always use `CommonValidatorFunctions`. The method does not check `spec`, and stops at the first failure. @param entity - The entity to check @returns The same entity object @throws An error that names the first field that has no value, fails its validator, or makes its validator throw

sites.rule: Summary: Sets the default parent on a group entity that has no parent. Remarks: The method leaves the entity unchanged if its `kind` is not exactly `Group`, compared case-sensitively, if `spec.parent` is already set, or if the entity is itself the default parent. Otherwise, it sets `spec.parent` to the canonical reference of the default parent that was passed to the constructor. It writes to the entity passed in, not to a copy. @param entity - The entity to update @returns The same entity object @throws A `TypeError` if an entity of kind `Group` has no `spec`, since the method does no validation of its own
